verdicts.claim: There are four checkpoint modes: PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE. PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting
verdicts.evidence: v2 doc: 'Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers... busy-handler callback is never invoked... might leave the checkpoint unfinished'. (Doc also lists a fifth NOOP mode, so 'four' is slightly incomplete.)

verdicts.evidence: v2 doc: 'FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock'; wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE... can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()'.

verdicts.evidence: v2 doc: 'until all readers are reading from the database file only... next writer will restart the log file'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes'; wal.html: 'readers might block while the checkpoint is running' (v2 doc says RESTART 'does not impede readers' — minor tension between the two SQLite pages).

verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete... avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps"'.

verdicts.evidence: Syncthing post (bt90, 2026-02-06): 'As our application level checkpointer is timer based, we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'; 'truncating the WAL requires no active readers/writers'.
